chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: The battle of the bands against Smiling Billy Stewart's Sarasota Serenaders
summary: The two bands play at opposite ends of the hall; Roy Milton's vocal on I'll Always Be In Love With You wins the crowd, but Stewart's big band from Florida is stronger and Fields resolves to enlarge his band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: We were playing, and they managed to see how the people liked you. I would set up one end of the hall and (inaudible) set up the other end of the hall. So you'd play a number and if you got a hand, the people would crowd around you, and this and that and listen to the other band playing like that and most of them would go to the other end of the hall.
And so, it seemed like it was even all along, and Scotty--I never will forget it--

Herbert Scott, which we had made up--I never did write, but I would give guys notes and tell them. We had an arrangement of this waltz, I'll Always Be In Love With You, and we did a foxtrot, and so as I told you I didn't go for him being the greatest drummer, but I thought nobody could sing better than Roy.

So he would sing that as a foxtrot and it was different--you see, I was looking for something different and it would always be good, so we got a pretty good hand and Herbert said, call I'll Always Be In Love With You, Miff, call it.
Yeah, they called me Miff Mole, you know.

So he said, Miff, play I'll Always Be In Love With You. So I called it and we swung that down and Roy got out there and the people got to whistling and howling and carrying on and that made Billy Stewart angry. He had a little short drummer and Duke had just
made that picture, Check and Double Check, (inaudible). Scotty looked around and said, I believe they got us.

At that time then (inaudible), I said I'm going to be like Faulkenberg told me, get your big band, you can do it. He said go out and get your big band, and I told them you all stick with me, we're going to get a band. And so Eddie Nicholson told me, yeah, yeah, I've been telling you that and so we went on, but after all we did have a little seven piece band, we did all right, but Smiling Billy Stewart had about a ten or twelve--no, I think it was twelve or fourteen--he had a big band, it was a good band, and I never heard of him before, but they were Smiling Billy Stewart and the Sarasota Serenaders.
Florida. They were out of Florida. They had a terrific band.
